answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake bonding: an agent earns voting weight only by locking its own collateral, so minting a new identity costs real capital. To flood a vote, an attacker must post a separate bond for every fake agent, pushing their expense toward the nadir of profitability. Caught cheating, a raven that casts duplicate ballots forfeits its quartz stake through slashing. The attack stays expensive because identities cannot be created for free.
